definitions.explanation: A number written as a whole number with a proper fraction beside it, such as 1 and 2/3. Japanese textbooks introduce it as the readable way of expressing a {仮分数|かぶんすう} (improper fraction).

examples.japanese: {答|こた}えを{帯分数|たいぶんすう}で{書|か}く。
examples.english: Write the answer as a mixed number.

examples.japanese: {帯分数|たいぶんすう}のほうが{大|おお}きさが{分|わ}かりやすい。
examples.english: It's easier to grasp the size when it's written as a mixed number.

examples.japanese: {帯分数|たいぶんすう}は{整数|せいすう}の{部分|ぶぶん}と{真分数|しんぶんすう}の{部分|ぶぶん}に{分|わ}けて{考|かんが}えると{計算|けいさん}しやすい。
examples.english: Mixed numbers are easier to calculate with if you think of them as a whole-number part and a proper-fraction part.

notes:
{帯|たい} (to wear, to carry alongside) + {分数|ぶんすう} (fraction): a fraction carrying a whole number with it.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {帯分数|たいぶんすう}に{直|なお}す: to convert into a mixed number
- {帯分数|たいぶんすう}で{表|あらわ}す: to express as a mixed number

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {仮分数|かぶんすう}: improper fraction — the same value written with a single numerator and denominator
- {真分数|しんぶんすう}: proper fraction — the fractional part of a mixed number
- {整数|せいすう}: whole number, integer — the part written to the left
